finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts::hand-rolled trim regex backtracks quadratically (redos) on attacker-controlled note content, replacing upstream's linear `.trim()`
evidence: Verified in the supplied packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts: lines 19–22 define `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` and `asciiTrim`, which is applied to `state.getLines(...)` in `lheadingRule` (the `const content = asciiTrim(...)` block, ~line 134), reachable from `NotePreview.render()` via `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` in preview.ts. The trailing alternative `[ws]+$` under `g` is the classic quadratic-trim ReDoS: `replace` retries at every offset, and inside a whitespace run not terminated by end-of-string each offset greedily consumes the run then backtracks char-by-char failing `$`, giving O(k²); upstream markdown-it's lheading uses linear `String.prototype.trim()`, so this path is newly introduced. I rate it minor rather than higher because it needs a deliberately crafted payload of tens-to-hundreds of KB of whitespace plus a setext underline, and the victim impact is a frozen browser tab in the preview pane (I could not confirm any server-side renderer shares this markdown-it instance); a smaller side effect is that the regex trims only ASCII whitespace where `.trim()` trimmed all Unicode whitespace.
